en: Praise of the Thirty-Sixfold Samvara:
With my whole being, I bow to the illustrious Saṃvara, the Great Hero, and also to the Yoginī Vārāhī—the leader of the host of Yoginīs. (1)
Likewise, [he visualizes] Ḍākinī, Lāmā, Khaṇḍarohā, and Rūpiṇī, as well as four vessels of nectar filled with the thought of awakening (bodhicitta). || 2 ||
I bow to the hero born of Pullīramalaya, who is the Saṃvara of Khaṇḍakapāla, embraced by Pracaṇḍā, and who resides upon my head. (3)
I bow to the heroic Mahākaṅkālasaṃvara, who has arisen from Jālandhara, who is embraced by Caṇḍālī, and who resides in the region of the crest-lock (śikhā). || 4 ||
I bow to the Saṃvara named Kaṅkāla, who has arisen from Oḍiyāna, who is in union with Prabhāvatī, and who resides in the right ear. (5)
I bow to Saṃvara, who dwells in the center of the Arbuda seat, possessing formidable fangs and endowed with a great nose, situated in the region of the back.
I bow to that which is born from the Godāvarī, the enclosure of the field of liquor (surāvīriṇa),
the casket known as Vīramatī, situated in the left ear.
I bow to the Hero born from Rāmeśvara, the Saṃvara known as Amitābha,
the Lord who is the union of the Dwarf and the Wrathful, situated between the two eyebrows.
I bow to the Lord born of Devīkoṭa, known as Vajraprabha-saṃvara, who is in union with Laṅkeśvarī and resides in the corner of the eye. 9.
I bow to the one who has entered the shade of the tree, who resides in the region of the aggregates, and who is the Saṃvara known as Vajradeha, arisen from that which is called Māra’s speech. 10.
I bow to the hero born from Kāmarūpa, known as Aṅgulika, who is the Samvara united with Airāvatī and resides in the armpit region. 11.
I bow to the Hero, born from the union of two bodies, who has arisen from the place of the syllable *oṃ*, who is the Vajra-jaṭila-saṃvara embraced by Bhairavī. 12.
I bow to the Lord born from Triśakuni, the Saṃvara known as Mahāvīra,
who has entered into Vāyuvegā and resides in the region of the navel.
I bow to the one born from the tip of the nose, who arose in Kauśalā as the Vajra-hūṃkāra-saṃvara, and who is in union with Surābhakṣī. 14.
I bow to the Saṃvara named Suprabha, born from the Kaliṅga-pīṭha, who has entered into Śyāmādevī and is produced from the region of the face. 15.
I bow to the hero named Vajraprabha-saṃvara, who is born in the place of Lampāka, who embraces Subhadrā, and who arises from the region of the throat. 16.
I bow to the Great Bhairava-Saṃvara, born from the sacred seat named Kāñcī, who has merged with Hayakarṇā and resides in the center of the heart. 17.
I bow to the hero born from the Himalayas, known as Virūpākṣa-Saṃvara,
who is in union with Khagānanā and resides in the region of the penis.
I bow to the one named Saṃvara Mahābala, who has arisen in Pretapuri, who has entered into Cakravega, and who resides in the station of the Liṅga. 19.
I bow to the Saṃvara known as Ratnavajra, who has arisen from the secret place, who is in union with Khaṇḍarohā, and who resides in the center of the anus. 20.
I bow to the hero named Hayagrīvasaṃvara, born in the land of Saurāṣṭra, who is embraced by Śauṇḍinī and resides in the center of the vulva. 21.
I bow to the one born on Suvarṇadvīpa, who possesses the vow of Ākāśagarbha, who is united with Cakravarmiṇī, and who resides in the middle of the shanks. 22.
I bow to the Hero named Śrī Heruka-Saṃvara, who dwells in the center of the city-pīṭha, embraced by Suvīrā, and who resides upon the finger. 23.
I bow to the one born in the land of Sindhu, known as Padmanṛtya-saṃvara, who has attained great power and stands upon the back of an elephant. 24.
I bow to the Saṃvara known as Vairocana, born from the Marutīpīṭha, who is in union with Cakravartinī and resides between the thumb and the middle finger. 25.
Born from Kulatā, the vow known as Vajrasattva, who has entered into the state of great heroism—bow down to him who resides between the two knees. 26.
I bow to the hero, the lord of the gods, named Vajracaṇḍa-saṃvara, who stands at the eastern gate and is embraced by Kākāsyā. || 27 ||
I bow to the leader of the yakṣas, known as Vajrānala-saṃvara, who resides in the center of the northern gate and is in union with Ulūkāsyā. || 28 ||
I bow to the hero named Vajroṣṇīṣa-saṃvara, who resides in the center of the western gate, embraced by Śvānāsyā, and who is the lord of serpents. (29)
I bow to Yamanāyaka, who stands in the middle of the southern gate, who is the Saṃvara of Vajrakuṇḍalinī, and who is embraced by Śūkarāsyā. || 30 ||
I bow to the leader of the fire [direction], known as Vajrayakṣa Saṃvara, who resides in the southeast quarter and is in union with Yamadāḍhī. || 31 ||
I bow to the Lord of Rākṣasas, who resides in the southwestern quarter, who is the Saṃvara known as Vajrakīla, and who is in union with Yamadūtī. (32)
I bow to the lord of the wind, who resides in the division of the northwest direction, is named Vajramahābala, and is joined with Yamadaṃṣṭrī.
I bow to the Lord of Beings, who resides in the northeastern quarter, who is the terrifying Vajrasaṃvara, and who is in union with Yamamathanī. (34)
I pay homage to these deities well-established in the cardinal and intermediate directions—to all the heroes, the heroines, and Heruka, the Supreme Lord. (35)
The deity, whose nature is innate bliss, is pure and engaged in the *tāṇḍava* dance;
situated in the midst of the network of *ḍākinīs*, he is the object of experience to be realized within oneself. (36)
Having praised this circle of goddesses, whatever merit has been acquired by me through this, by that merit may the world be devoted to Vajraḍāka. (37)
The *Śrī-Ṣaṭtriṃśat-saṃvara-gaṇacakra-maṇḍala-stuti* is completed.
